Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s newly introduced era lift-off

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his fresh kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.
  • Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.
  • Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his fresh kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0.

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

Sources indicate that mcGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo.

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery stated: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”.

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Recent findings suggest that their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim.

It has been revealed that villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1.

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Sources indicate that club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu.

Industry observers note that villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a upcoming Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7.

In a recent development, villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Sources indicate that slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Sources indicate that really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A significant let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Abraham replaces goalscorer Jackson.

Industry observers note that villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

According to recent reports, yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Industry observers note that hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

It has been revealed that villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

According to recent reports, virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Recent findings suggest that villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Industry observers note that club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Recent findings suggest that brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘fresh’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

It has been revealed that brugge are just reminding Villa that they are still there. Virgili is at the heart of things again, combining with Vetlesen who works the ball out to Forbs whose cross is well held by Suzuki.

Villa then spring forward, Hemmings breaching the Brugge box, but Buendia’s eventual effort does not make it through a thicket of legs.

Recent findings suggest that brugge are building with a three-man backline, sending Siquet forward high and wide. They’ve had much of the ball in the opening stages of this half, which is probably part of Villa’s strategy. Emery’s side have settled into an out-of-possession 4-4-2.

In a recent development, vanakan is booked for simulation after going hitting the deck off a challenge from Gomes. There is a knowing smile on the Belgian midfielder’s face which suggests the referee’s convictions were correct.

In a recent development, we are back under way... Siquet replaces Sabbe at the interval.

Nicolas Jackson is off the mark for Aston Villa. He beat Yann Sommer to the ball, held off a defender and was left with the simplest of finishes to round off a fine first half for Villa. pic.twitter.com/gWx6kUTlOX.

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

Recent findings suggest that this has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

Recent findings suggest that it’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson races on to a nothing punt over the top by Torres, and the situation appears under control with two defenders in the striker’s orbit, but Sommer comes steaming out and Jackson nudges the ball past him before sliding it home into a vacant net.

Industry observers note that jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0.

In a recent development, A sloppy Torres pass out from the back goes straight to Vetlesen who picks out Forbs first time. The winger unleashes an effort from range but Suzuki makes a smart stop.

There is a shout for a Villa handball as Virgili prods a cross on to Kamara’s body, but his arms are clearly by his side.

Villa are presented with a great opportunity to break but the pass in behind for Jackson to gallop on to does not have enough juice and the move breaks down. Jackson does have a sight at goal moments later, but he’s only able to poke the ball wide off a free-kick from the right.

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Brugge have certainly not given up the ghost, still looking to work the ball out to Forbs and Virgili on the flanks. Sabbe overlaps down the right but his ball to Vetlesen is cut out and Villa attempt to spring a counter which is snuffed out by Mechele.

Villa midfielder Joao Gomes is having a productive evening as he aims to recover from that nightmare debut.

He was sent off after 40 minutes of his first Villa appearance in the excruciating 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Wan-Bissaka drives down the right as Villa look for a third, but his cross is overhit and goes off on the far side. The right intent, though.

According to recent reports, club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 2 (Buendia) Jackson holds up the ball expertly before slipping in Gomes. The midfielder bursts into the box, outwitting Vetlesen before cutting the ball back to an onrushing Buendia who clips the ball past Sommer with aplomb. A crazy couple of minutes!

Recent findings suggest that vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim.

It is now nervy in the stadium and the Brugge fans are already starting to boo some of their players.

Villa’s first goal of the season and no surprise it comes from their talisman John McGinn.

Recent findings suggest that close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Industry observers note that goalkeeper Sommer is penalised for handling the ball outside of his box. He had gathered a corner and had stormed forward to set off an attack. He changes his mind mid-throw and attempts to re-catch the ball but ends up wandering outside of his allotted space. The resulting free-kick crashes straight into the wall.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ.

Industry observers note that club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. He offloads the ball to McGinn on the right of the area and the Scotsman steadies himself before curling the ball into the far post, beyond Sommer.

Recent findings suggest that it is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a fresh team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,.

The £30m signing from Parma possesses a wide passing range and much of Villa’s build-up play starts with the Japan international.

He is Villa’s very own version of Manchester City’s former pass master Ederson.

Much has been made of Suzuki’s distribution and he has already teased a couple of lovely flighted balls up-field. Villa’s defenders are more than happy to lure Brugge’s first line of pressure forward but have not yet been able to find an incisive line-breaking pass.

Seyes and Virgili combine down the left in Brugge’s best attack so far, but Torres is able to head behind for a corner, which is not up to much.

Wan-Bissaka has taken up a very aggressive position down Villa’s right and he earns a free-kick in a promising position. McGinn spins in a delivery which is only partially cleared but Maatsen’s effort from the edge of the box is smothered.

Villa get their foot on the ball from the get-go, circulating the ball around the back, before Suzuki debuts a long ball up to Wan-Bissaka. The ball is worked to McGinn who feeds Buendia on the edge of the box but his effort flies just wide.

There is a minute’s silence for those affected by the floods in Nepal which is impeccably observed.

The players then retreat to their halves and Jackson gets us going!

As the rain lashes down in Bruges, you get the sense that Villa will have to dig deep to get a result and breathe life into their season. Both teams thrive on attacking transitions and the surface-level moisture will encourage breakaway moves.

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his latest team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

In a recent development, brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:.

Industry observers note that don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too substantial and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

Recent findings suggest that in Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today declared as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

It has been revealed that christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

Recent findings suggest that while Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Club Brugge Sommer; Sabbe, Lee, Mechele, Seys; Potts, Vanaken; Forbs, Vetlesen, Virgili; Tresoldi.

Substitutes Abraham, Barkley, Bizot, Bogarde, Garnacho, Mbaye, Mings, Ruggeri, Wright, Alysson.

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle matter so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He mentioned: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

Industry observers note that “We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now fresh players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [significant] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

Industry observers note that “We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a upcoming test.”.

According to recent reports, the experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

According to recent reports, emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi.

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a newly introduced-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s upcoming-look crew.

Industry observers note that morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his upcoming recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Sources indicate that although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

According to recent reports, directeur commercial du Stade de Reims, Fabrice Harvey évoque dans L'Union le match que les Verts joueront demain soir à Delaune. Extraits.

It has been revealed that "C'est très clairement le match de l'année. Il y a toujours une ferveur incroyable autour des Verts, qui attirent toujours autant que ce soit en Ligue 2 ou en Ligue 1. Ça demeure une affiche de notre championnat qui a marqué le temps et qui a traversé les époques. Il y a une vraie demande. On a vendu des places VIP supplémentaires, 20 à 25% en plus que lors d'un match ordinaire.

Sources indicate that les joueurs vont devoir être bons sur le terrain, à nous de l'être également dans les salons. On va mettre les petits plats dans les grands pour accueillir le mieux possible les partenaires. On veut montrer qu'on peut faire du business autour du Stade de Reims. C'est l'opportunité d'attirer de nouveaux sponsors jusqu'à la fin de saison. On a envie de leur proposer une belle soirée, qu'ils soient contents d'être venus pour ce match-là et que ça leur donne envie de revenir.".

  • It has been revealed that nos difficultés rencontrées parfois à l’extérieur ne sont pas liées à une question d’être à domicile ou à l’extérieur, mais simplement à la façon dont l’adversaire a  su jouer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

En conférence de presse hier Ian Cathro, après avoir réfuté toute difficulté de son groupe à performer à l’extérieur, s’est longuement exprimé sur sa gestion de l’effectif, afin de maintenir tout le monde à disposition et est revenu plus précisément sur le cas de son métronome hongrois, Aron Csongvai :.

« On se prépare pour un gros match, un match contre un adversaire très fort. Un match qu’on aborde avec beaucoup de motivation, beaucoup d’ambition. Je ne sais pas si le match sera spectaculaire. Je m’en fiche. Gagner me suffit. On aime tous le foot aussi, et c’est beau quand il y a des bons joueurs sur le terrain. Ça sera un gros match, et on est excité à l’idée de jouer un gros match de foot.

It has been revealed that nos difficultés rencontrées parfois à l’extérieur ne sont pas liées à une question d’être à domicile ou à l’extérieur, mais simplement à la façon dont l’adversaire a  su jouer. C’était le cas à Dijon, même si on a gagné, à Dunkerque même si il était très étrange de perdre ce match . Mais les difficultés venaient plus de la façon dont l’adversaire a su nous déséquilibrer que du fait de jouer à l’extérieur. Peut-être que le seul match où le fait de ne pas jouer à domicile a eu un impact était la fin de match à Metz, parce que là l’ambiance a pu jouer.

Contre Rumilly, j’ai préféré notre seconde période à la première. On avait 10 joueurs absents. C’était difficile d’avoir une équipe avec du rythme car les joueurs avaient eu très peu de temps pour trouver des automatismes, peut-être deux entraînements ensemble. La défense a trois a été une option. Je suis très à l’aise avec la défense à trois qui peut être une option bien utile. La seule chose à laquelle je suis marié c’est ma femme. Mon job est d’aider les joueurs à gagner. Une saison de foot est longue. Et ça se joue aussi en fonction des joueurs disponibles. On manage beaucoup le temps de jeu des joueurs pour éviter les problèmes. Donc on doit toujours avoir une option alternative.

Industry observers note that parfois connaître la personne aide à mieux connaître le footballeur. Aron Csongvai fait de l’excellent boulot, il s’est adapté très vite. C’est un mec mature. Il est à une étape de sa vie où il était parfaitement prêt à franchir cette étape, changer de vie, venir dans un plus grand club. N’oublions pas que sa saison a démarré en janvier, ce n’est pas facile. Mais oui il fait vraiment un boulot très notable pour l’équipe. Son rôle c’est de garder l’équilibre avec ou sans le ballon. Il a une grosse responsabilité dans le fait que l’équipe reste équilibrée. L’objectif est de le garder en forme sur les 2 ou 3 mois à venir car je le répète il vient d’une compétition qui a démarré en janvier. Quand les autres clôtureront une saison complète, lui il bouclera une saison ½ de compétition. Donc ce que j’attends de lui c’est qu’il parvienne à rester en forme parce qu’il joue un rôle important dans notre organisation. Donc gardons le en bonne santé et essayons quand c’est possible de lui permettre de se reposer un peu.

Are you the most knowledgeable football fan around? Do you want to be involved with EA SPORTS FIFA? Well, you’re in luck as the FIFA Talent Scout team is looking for people like you.

The FIFA Talent Scout community has over 6000 active members and is always looking for individuals to help improve their football database.

This is a great opportunity to put your knowledge of your club to good use, helping to ensure that the EA SPORTS football database continues to contain the most up to date and accurate team and player data for the many leagues featured in FIFA 17.

The first step into our community is as a football analyst, who can examine team and player data and offer feedback suggesting possible changes. You can contribute towards improving player appearance, player attributes, team formations and team tactics. There is no minimum or maximum expectation in terms of your contribution to the database. The key is that when you do contribute, your feedback helps to improve the authenticity of FIFA 17.

According to recent reports, those who stand out may be offered the chance to join our editing team and the chance to take full responsibility for a team and its squad. We are able to offer some financial compensation to editors, but in return we do require that you are a very active contributor who works to our deadlines and in line with our guidelines.

http://fifa-talentscout.ea.com/.

Stay in the conversation with FIFA Talent Scout by following: https://twitter.com/FIFATALENTSCOUT.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Feyenoord preserved their four-point advantage over champions PSV after coming away with a point from Eindhoven thanks to an improved second-half performance.

PSV dominated the first half as they deployed a close-passing, tiki-taka style to stifle Feyenoord, but only had Guus Til’s well-taken volley after 20 minutes to show for it.

Ten minutes after the break Feyenoord equalised when Anis Hadj Moussa was given too much space to charge down the right flank and bend a shot inside the far post.

The Algerian had a good chance for a second towards the end, while PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar had to be alert to keep out a header by Nacho Ferri from close range.

Sources indicate that “We were by far the better team today and had the better chances,” said PSV coach Peter Bosz. “We started the second half badly and made a mistake, after which Hadj Moussa scored. And even then we could have won it.”.

Ajax overtook PSV to close the gap at the top to three points with a hard-fought win at Sparta. Veteran striker Jens Toornstra scored for Sparta on his 500th Eredivisie appearance, but Abdellah Ouazane and Tolu Arokodare, the scorers against Atalanta in midweek, were on target again to claim the win for Ajax.

Twente moved up to fourth place as two late goals by Sondre Ørjasæter and Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink earned a 2-0 win at AZ Alkmaar, who like Twente and PSV have 20 points.

Fortuna Sittard also snatched the points late on against Excelsior as Rodrigo Guth headed in a corner in injury time to keep the Limburg club in sixth place, two points further back.

At the other end of the table, the return of Adrie Koster as veteran coach brought no relief to Willem II, who crashed to a 6-1 home defeat to Cambuur.

The Tilburgers remain four points behind ADO Den Haag, who were unable to keep up the momentum of last week’s win against PSV as they lost 3-2 at home to Heerenveen.

Telstar lost by the same margin at Go Ahead Eagles, whose striker Søren Tengstedt netted twice in the first half to lead the Eredivisie scoring charts with eight goals.

Willem II Tilburg 1-6 Cambuur Leeuwarden.

Sources indicate that we kick off by alerting you to a superb interview in the Guardian by Nick Ames with Port Vale's Portuguese manager Bruno Ribeiro. Benfica are top of the Liga NOS and their coach Rui Vitória continues to confound the doubters who believed he would not be up to the job at the Lisbon giants. Simon Curtis takes a look at "the quiet man at the helm of a national institution". And Benfica fans, while we've got your attention, a shout out for Tom Kundert's profile of the club's world-renowned Seixal Academy for ESPN.

Talking about Portuguese football schools, none has produced more top-class players in recent decades than Sporting's Alcochete Academy, and the excellent Outside of the Boot website has a brilliantly detailed profile written by Mateus Carvalho of another possible gem for the Lions, Francisco Geraldes, who is currently on loan at Moreirense.

In a recent development, to finish up this initial trip around the net, we alert you to FourFourTwo's list of the 59 best Under-21 footballers from around the world. The section we highlight has a mini profile of Porto striker André Silva, who will be hoping to net his first senior international goal tonight for the Seleção against Andorra. In case you're wondering, the British magazine rank him at number 23.

C’est sans doute notre plus grand talent depuis Hugo Ekitike. » Parmi les observateurs, la question est de mesurer à quel point la séquence actuelle représente fidèlement son niveau. « Oui, ça l’est. Il a un sens du but et du déplacement assez épatant. C’est un garçon déjà assez complet, capable de jouer dans plein de positions différentes. Il a un vrai profil. » analyse Hervé Renard, son sélectionneur (…) Reims n’entend pas perdre son talent cet hiver. A moins qu’un club ne formule une offre avec un prêt immédiat dans l’effectif champenois. « Il ne vaut pas moins que Patrick Zabi vendu 25M€ au Paris FC l’été dernier) » estime-t-on au club (…) « Il faudra qu’il passe par une étape avant d’aller plus haut. Sports club members becoming less tolerant of homosexuality

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents said they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute mentioned the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF said the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, stated it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”.

Comme l'avait fait l'avant-veille La Dernière Heure Les Sports +, la RTBF a abordé hier la course à la succession du néo-retraité international Romelu Lukaku. Extraits.

Sources indicate that "Le style d’attaquant ultra-puissant, fort dos au but, dangereux de la tête, redoutable finisseur va désormais manquer en équipe nationale. On se penche vers nos jeunes promesses pour tenter de retrouver ce type de buteur qui pèse sur une défense et qui nous a souvent sortis d’une impasse ces dernières années. Chez les moins de 21 ans, les perspectives restent prometteuses pour occuper ce rôle de pur n°9 : trois buteurs déjà bien connus se disputent deux places dans le onze de base de Gill Swerts : Lucas Stassin, Roméo Vermant et Norman Bassette. Robin Mirisola (OHL, prêté par Genk) reste une alternative à garder à l’œil, lui qui a inscrit récemment deux buts contre l’Italie en amical.

Quatre jeunes buteurs au profil intéressant… mais différent de celui de Romelu Lukaku dont la puissance pouvait faire valser dans le décor n’importe quel défenseur une fois lancé vers le but. Stassin et Vermant ont été convoqués une seule fois par Rudi Garcia. Bassette, lui, a été appelé une fois sous l’ère Domenico Tedesco. A titre de comparaison, lorsqu’il avait 21 ans, Big Rom comptait déjà 11 buts avec les Diables Rouges. Preuve une nouvelle fois de sa précocité et de son efficacité inédite sous la vareuse noire-jaune-rouge. Les souliers laissés par Romelu sont sans doute encore un peu trop grands pour ces trois-là.

In a recent development, dans les catégories d’âge inférieures, un joueur a crevé l’écran ces derniers mois : Jeoffrey Mbambi. Tout juste âgé de 15 ans, le Belge est en train d’affoler les compteurs. En 5 rencontres, l’avant-centre a trouvé 9 fois le fond des filets (dont quatre doublés) pour les U17 où il est surclassé. En 364 minutes jouées, soit un but toutes les 40 minutes en moyenne ! Puissant, rapide, un sens du but déjà aiguisé, les similitudes sur le terrain entre Mbambi et Lukaku sont frappantes. Physiquement aussi, le Diablotin mesure déjà 1m86.

Des ressemblances aussi dans le parcours et les origines. Né à Vilvorde, Jeoffrey grandit dans une famille de footeux. Le Belgo-Congolais est le frère cadet de Jérémy Mbambi (18 ans), qui évolue à Saint-Trond, et Jediaél Mbambi (17 ans), son autre frère, qui a signé son premier contrat professionnel à Saint-Etienne [ce dernier n'a joué cette saison qu'un seul match de N2 - lors de la 1ère journée - et 3 avec les U19 nationaux, le dernier il y a 2 mois pile poil, ndp2] . Cet été, repéré par le Club Bruges, Jeoffrey Mbambi a paraphé son premier contrat pro en Venise du Nord, le liant aux Blauw & Zwart jusqu’en 2029.

Industry observers note that dans le noyau des U18, l’adaptation s’est bien déroulée puisque le Brabançon a disputé 8 rencontres et planté 7 buts. Des débuts plus que prometteurs à 15 ans, faut-il encore le rappeler, qui lui permettent de s’entraîner de temps à autre avec le Club NXT, les U23 évoluant en Challenger Pro League. Jeoffrey Mbambi ne devrait pas tarder avant de faire ses débuts dans le football professionnel belge. Certaines rumeurs l’envoient déjà dans les plus grands clubs européens à l’affût.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cela faisait 25 jours que Laurent Peyrelade avait été limogé par la Direction du SEC Bastia. Les dirigeants du club corse ont pris leur temps mais, surtout, ont voulu se donner le maximum de réflexion. Plusieurs noms ont circulé avant l'officialisation du nouveau coach qui sera Ghislain Printant, ainsi que l'indique Corse-Matin. Le SEC Bastia n'a pas tardé a apporter la confirmation. Dans le même communiqué, le club indique, tout en le remerciant, que Michel Moretti reste à son poste d'adjoint.

It has been revealed that "L'arrivée de Ghislain Printant ne doit donc rien à l'improvisation, encore moins à la précipitation. Le coach qui a fait monter le Sporting à Paris pour la finale de la Coupe de la Ligue, en avril 2015, a toujours clamé son amour du club, y compris lorsqu'il a été démis de ses fonctions en janvier 2016 au profit de son adjoint d'alors, François Ciccolini.Loyal, certes, mais aussi compétent puisqu'au-delà de ses premières fonctions de formateur, il a longtemps été un entraîneur adjoint, à Montpellier, bien sûr, mais aussi à Marseille, à Saint-Etienne, avec la sélection de Côte d'Ivoire, toujours avec son ami de longue date, le regretté Jean-Louis Gasset.".

Sources indicate that le quotidien précise : "Certes, le club a changé depuis son passage entre 2010 et 2016, époque durant laquelle il a connu Gilles Cioni, l'actuel coordinateur sportif du Sporting. Pour autant, lors d'un récent entretien avec notre titre, il avait démontré qu'il suivait toujours l'actualité du club, d'autant que son fils, Florian, y était entraîneur des gardiens avant de s'engager avec Evian-Thonon. Le nouveau coach du Sporting devrait bien évidemment être dans les travées d'Armand-Cesari pour le match face à Villefranche, ce samedi 21 novembre. Lundi il devrait diriger sa première séance et tenir une conférence de presse de présentation.".

Recent findings suggest that ghislain Printant était arrivé à l'ASSE en décembre 2017, comme adjoint de  Jean-Louis Gasset. Le duo succédait à Oscar Garcia, Julien Sablé ayant assuré un interim de 35 jours. Après une belle fin de saison 2017-2018, et une non moins belle saison 2018-2019, ponctuée par une 4ème place qualificative pour l'Europa League, il a été nommé entraîneur principal de l'ASSE, le 6 juin 2019, suite au départ de Jean-Louis Gasset. Mais le début de saison 2019-2020 est mitigé et son contrat sera résilié le 4 octobre 2019, laissant la place à Claude Puel.

Quelques mois plus tard, le 10 août 2020, Ghislain Printant va rejoindre son ami Jean-Louis Gasset et devenir son adjoint aux Girondins de Bordeaux.

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he said. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”.

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Sources indicate that excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop said the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 4-0 Go Ahead Eagles.

Top five football betting tips and tricks

📅 31 Aug 2018 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well.
  • Getting started on football betting is far from easy, though.
  • It has been revealed that but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

Getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

It has been revealed that but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

Industry observers note that you might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having said that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

In this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

An obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it important to follow the action closely?

It has been revealed that first of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more notable, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

As you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

As you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits.

It has been revealed that favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

Industry observers note that if you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Industry observers note that finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier said than done, though.

Industry observers note that whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

Sous contrat avec l'ASSE jusqu'en juin 2029 mais prêté cette saison au FC Séville (avec une option d'achat estimée à 25 M€), Lucas Stassin s'est brièvement confié à DAZN avant le derby contre le Betis programmé ce samedi à 18h30.

Industry observers note that "On est 6e de Liga, je trouve que c'est un bon début de saison. Maintenant, on peut toujours faire mieux. Quand on regarde les matches où on a perdu des points, ça se joue toujours à des petits détails. Il faut voir le positif, on est dans le top 6 et on va essayer de rester dedans toute la saison. Franchement on m'a très bien accueilli. Le team manager ici est très, très cool. Il parle français en plus. je me suis très vite adapté au groupe. Il y a d'autres francophones dans le groupe [notamment Arouna Sangante, Lucien Agoumé et Youssouf Fofana, ndp2], on parle du championnat de France, forcément. On peut parler français entre nous, c'est cool de parler la langue maternelle. On parle des clubs par où on est passé et des joueurs contre qui on a joué.

Sources indicate that je garde un très, très bon souvenir de Saint-Etienne parce que j'y ai quand même passé une belle saison en Ligue 1 avec un bon derby forcément. Je garde un très bon souvenir de mes coéquipiers et du staff même s'ils ont changé beaucoup de staff. En Espagne, il y-a forcément les trois grosses équipes [Barça, Real, Atletico, ndp2] alors qu'en France il y a moins ça, chaque année est un peu différente. En Espagne les duels sont quand même un peu plus intensifs. La mentalité est différente sur le terrain, c'est vraiment toujours à 200% du début jusqu'à la fin du match. Techniquement, il y a énormément de bons joueurs en Liga même si en France il y avait déjà énormément de qualités, ça m'avait impressionné quand j'étais arrivé.

Sources indicate that le derby sévillan, on m'en a parlé depuis que je suis là. On en parle beaucoup. On sait que c'est un très, très gros derby. Avec Lyon et Saint-Etienne, je sais forcément l'ambiance qu'il pourrait y avoir, l'enthousiasme, donc j'ai vraiment hâte de voir comment va être l'ambiance ici. On veut surtout essayer de gagner ce derby pour passer une bonne soirée et une bonne semaine. On se prépare beaucoup, on parle beaucoup de ça à l'entraînement. On va aborder ce match avec une bonne envie. Si le fait de pouvoir me distinguer lors du derby peut être notable et intéressant dans la perspective d'être rappelé chez les Diables Rouges ? Ouais, forcément, on a toujours l'objectif de performer en club pour être repris en équipe nationale. La prochaine sélection est en mars, je vais tout faire d'ici-là pour essayer d'avoir des chances d'être repris.".

Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4847 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.
  • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.
  • It has been revealed that he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

It has been revealed that he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he mentioned.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

Given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

That was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a latest manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

It has been revealed that moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

It has been revealed that playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

Recent findings suggest that there were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

It has been revealed that millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

Millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

Newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

According to recent reports, so much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

Well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil stated: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

Industry observers note that “We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

As for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

The draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

Sources indicate that the third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:.

Crystal Palace 3-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” mentioned Willock after the match.

“100% [the competition is crucial], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a new coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a significant game in keeping that momentum.”.

"We stated at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT.

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:.

It has been revealed that moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

In a recent development, seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

According to recent reports, newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

Finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

You can hear the travelling fans now!

Marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Sources indicate that issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Recent findings suggest that millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

Sources indicate that double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

In a recent development, free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

What colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

It has been revealed that it’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Industry observers note that newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

Industry observers note that millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

According to recent reports, the game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

It has been revealed that the delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

According to recent reports, gonzález is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

Recent findings suggest that millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Sources indicate that newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

Sources indicate that I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

First piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

It has been revealed that barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

Wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

In a recent development, newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

It has been revealed that another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

Industry observers note that murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

According to recent reports, newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

Fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge.

Starting XI: Lukás Hornícek; Lewis Hall, Fabian Schär, Amar Dedic, Sven Botman; Jacob Murphy, Nico González; Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock; Yoane Wissa.

Substitutes: Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, Malick Thiaw, Nick Pope, Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Touré, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur.

The teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

Alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach says has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

At the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.
